name: Damilola Mike-Bamiloye
history: Damilola Mike-Bamiloye is a Nigerian Christian filmmaker and the first child of Mike and Gloria Bamiloye. Mount Zion’s film profile says his interest began in childhood by acting out his father’s films, then copying scripts and developing into writing his own movies. His work spans feature films and serial dramas, including The Train, Legion, 30 Pieces, Shackles, Stranded, Magdalene and the Corpers’ Lodge series. The directory distinguishes titles listed in the filmography from direct video links and verified original posters.
imageAlt: Professional studio portrait of Damilola Mike-Bamiloye

name: John Oguntuase
history: John Oguntuase is a Nigerian faith-based filmmaker and the CEO of 2nd Touch Production. The Gospel Filmmaking Network describes him as a director, producer, actor and author, with about two decades of experience and more than 15 national and international awards. His work includes both short films and feature-length gospel stories.
productions: 2nd Touch Production / Peculiar Priesthood Production / JITA Studios

name: Mike Ilemobola
history: Mike Ilemobola's channel presents gospel movies intended to edify and comfort viewers. Gospelwood now includes the verified films Anchor and Open Heaven, with direct video links and YouTube thumbnail artwork. The catalogue can grow as additional video-level titles are checked.

name: Felix Bankole
history: Felix Bankole's current directory entries connect his work with Vision Drama Missions Outreach International and faith-based drama missions. Gospelwood documents the film titles and production credits that are available in its source records, while leaving unconfirmed release details unasserted.
productions: Mount Zion Institute North Zone / Felix Bankole
Vision Drama Missions Outreach International / NOSPLEJ Media Lagos
Vision Drama Missions Outreach International / Light Ministries International

name: Mike and Gloria Bamiloye
history: The directory's Mount Zion records trace a long-running Nigerian Christian-film tradition from Agbara Nla (1993) and The Perilous Times (1992) through later productions. Mike and Gloria Bamiloye are credited on several foundational titles; Damilola Mike-Bamiloye and other collaborators appear in the later generation of the archive.

name: EVOM World Network
history: EVOM World Network is represented in Gospelwood through a broad group of Nigerian Christian-film records, including My Conclusion, The Missing Link, On Strike, Blind But Loved, Revealed and Emi Fun Emi. Several catalogue entries do not identify an individual director in the available source data, so the spotlight credits the production community rather than guessing a filmmaker.

name: Mike Bamiloye
history: Mike Bamiloye is one of the foundational figures in Nigeria’s Christian-film movement and co-founded Mount Zion Film Productions with Gloria Bamiloye. Gospelwood’s records credit him on early and later Mount Zion productions. The profile keeps to the credits available in the directory and links to the production archive for further reading.

name: Gloria Bamiloye
history: Gloria Bamiloye is a co-founder of Mount Zion Film Productions and a long-standing contributor to Nigerian Christian drama and film. The directory credits her on foundational Mount Zion titles. This profile records the film credits available here without guessing at unverified biographical details.

name: Isaac Femi-Akintunde
history: Isaac Femi-Akintunde is named in Gospelwood’s current film records. The available catalogue provides limited biographical detail, so this spotlight focuses on his recorded credits and does not add an unverified career history.

name: John 316 Film School Foundation
history: Ugandan Christian film training institution founded by Bamulanzeki Geoffrey (VJ Geoffrey). Its official biography says the school grew from a vision to translate and distribute Christian movies to local communities and was formally established in 2022 to train creative professionals in onscreen storytelling.

name: KAC Studios
history: Ghana-based Christian-inspired studio whose team develops faith-rooted stories with broad audience appeal. Ghana News Agency reports that the studio screened The Cleaner, Mirage and The Right to Do Anything at an Accra industry event, with a stated ambition to combine Christian values with cinematic quality and everyday human themes.

name: M. D. Neely
history: M. D. Neely is named in one of the film records currently held by Gospelwood. Public biographical details were not established from the available project sources, so the profile keeps the credit precise and avoids inventing a biography.

name: Damilola Fasesan
history: Damilola Fasesan is named in Gospelwood’s current film records. The available project sources do not provide a verified biography, so this profile presents the existing credit without adding unsupported career claims.

name: Matrid Nyagah
organization: Fearless Films / African Christian Visual Media Network
history: Kenyan filmmaker, pastor and storyteller with more than a decade of experience in faith-driven film and immersive media. ICVM describes her as co-founder and executive director of Fearless Films, a mentor to creatives, and a founding member of the African Christian Visual Media Network. The directory includes her credited work on Where the River Divides; other widely known credits are listed as context, not automatically treated as Christian films.
imageAlt: Portrait available through the linked ICVM profile

name: Abel Waweru
history: Kenyan filmmaker and editor who founded the Christian International Film Festival Africa. The Standard reports that he has more than 13 years of film and media experience and conceived CIFFA as a bridge between professional filmmaking and Christian faith. His work connects filmmakers and audiences around faith-based storytelling across the continent.
imageAlt: Portrait available in the linked CIFFA launch report

name: Joyce Musoke
history: Joyce Musoke was identified by The Standard among the filmmakers participating in the inaugural Christian International Film Festival Africa in Nairobi in December 2025. The available report supports her participation in the faith-film community, but does not provide enough verified biographical detail to make stronger claims here.
filmography: Get Rich Quick (festival programme; director credit requires confirmation)
productions: Christian International Film Festival Africa participant
imageAlt: Portrait available in the linked CIFFA launch report

name: Sam Rushimisha
country: Rwanda / DR Congo (based in the United States)
history: Gospel artist Sam Rushimisha, born in DR Congo and raised in Rwanda, introduced his first Christian film Muri Yesu in 2025. InyaRwanda reports that it was released in Kinyarwanda, Swahili, English and Spanish. His profile represents the growing multilingual reach of Christian screen storytelling across African communities and the diaspora.
imageAlt: Public portrait of Sam Rushimisha from Isibo Media coverage

name: Chim Onyebilanma
history: The African Christian Visual Media Network describes Chim Onyebilanma as a filmmaker and member of the International Academy of Television Arts & Sciences. Through CAP Studios in Durban, he focuses on faith-based Afrocentric stories; the network notes that his feature Treasure Hunt had a South African theatrical release in 2025.
imageAlt: Portrait available through the linked ACVMN profile

name: Daniel James Ofori-Atta
history: Daniel James Ofori-Atta leads KAC Studios, a Christian-inspired production studio working to make faith-rooted stories accessible to audiences beyond church communities. Ghana News Agency reports that KAC Studios screened The Cleaner, Mirage and The Right to Do Anything at an Accra industry event, and describes its mission as combining Christian values with relatable, culturally grounded storytelling.
imageAlt: Portrait available in the linked Ghana News Agency report

name: Ayobami Adegboyega
history: Ayobami Adegboyega leads PRODRAM Productions, a faith-based film and drama ministry. PRODRAM describes its work as Christ-centred storytelling focused on biblical truth, family restoration and discipleship. Its official site lists productions including Nicodemeus, Forty XL and Faded Lines.

name: Olabimpe Adegboyega
history: Olabimpe Adegboyega is a co-producer and creative leader at PRODRAM Productions. The ministry credits her with helping shape stories around marriage, family, Christian womanhood and restoration, including the Husband and Wife Series.
imageAlt: Portrait available through the linked PRODRAM profile
